outcome: duration of active phase of labor (1st and 2nd stage)
finding: Epidural analgesia was found to be a safe and effective method of pain relief during labor, with no significant difference in operative delivery rates, labor duration, or need for oxytocin compared to the control group.
mod_finding: Epidural analgesia did not significantly affect the mode of delivery, with comparable rates of vaginal delivery (88% vs. 84%) and cesarean section (8% vs. 6%) in the epidural and control groups, respectively.
